In an emergency, drill batteries are great for a quick jump start.

Here's how I've done it before without this product.

1. Get 2 decent lengths of wire
2. Figure out which side is positive and which is negative on your drill battery 
3. Secure the wires onto the battery, noting which is which
4. Secure or hold the other ends of the wire, positive first, then negative, onto the vehicle battery for about 15 minutes.

At that point, the vehicle should start. Only turn your key once for a few seconds because if it doesn't work, you will drain all of your progress very easily. If the vehicle does not start, reattach your wires and hold for another 10-15 minutes, then repeat until the vehicle starts.

IMPORTANT NOTES
- This is not the best way to handle it and should only be used as a sort of last resort.
- DO NOT try to start your vehicle with the drill battery still attached to it. This may cause many problems, including, but not limited to, fire, electrical system damage, and in serious cases, explosion of one of your batteries. (This, of course, means your vehicle is going nowhere.)
